title: Affine-space ambient adjunction
statement:
Let $N\geq1$ be an integer, let $A$ be a finite commutative ring with $NA=0$, and let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], meaning one admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], on which $N$ is invertible. Let $d\in\mathbb N$ and let $p_d:\mathbf A^d_S\to S$ be the affine-space projection [def-sbc-affine-space]. Work on the small etale sites with the entire ordinary unbounded derived categories of constant-$A$ module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. The functor $p_d^*=p_d^{-1}$ is exact inverse image applied termwise to complexes [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Use the ordinary finite etale Tate sheaves [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]
$$A_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_T}A_T,\qquad A_T(0)=A_T,\qquad A_T(d)=A_T(1)^{\otimes_{A_T}d}\quad(d>0),$$
where $\mu_{N,T}(U)=\{z\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)^\times:z^N=1\}$, and write $K(d)=K\otimes_A^LA_T(d)$ using the ordinary derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Define ordinary etale compact supports by a compactification as in [def-amb-etale-compact-support], with the compactification-independent identification on these whole categories supplied by [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons]. There is an adjunction
$$Rp_{d!}:D((\mathbf A^d_S)_{\mathrm{et}},A)\ \rightleftarrows\ D(S_{\mathrm{et}},A):p_d^*(-)(d)[2d],\qquad Rp_{d!}\dashv p_d^*(-)(d)[2d].$$
In particular, the assertion imposes no boundedness or constructibility condition on either argument.

proof.text: Put $X_r=\mathbf A^r_S$, $X_0=S$, and let $a_r:X_r\to X_{r-1}$ forget the last coordinate. On $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ the identification $R[x_1,\ldots,x_r]=R[x_1,\ldots,x_{r-1}][x_r]$ identifies $a_r$ with the affine-line projection over $X_{r-1}$; these identifications respect restriction and hence glue [def-sbc-affine-space]. The polynomial algebras are finitely generated, and the diagonal is cut out by $x_i\otimes1-1\otimes x_i$, so these projections are finite type and separated by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Thus every $X_r$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. The image of a unit under a ring map is a unit, so $N$ remains invertible on them. For any such base $T$, the standard chart [lemma-nagata-relative-affine-space-open-immersion] and projective-space properness [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper] give $\mathbf A^r_T\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^r_T\to T$, a compactification in the sense of [def-asd-compactifiable]. The middle scheme is Noetherian: its proper projection is finite type, so apply the same Noetherian lemma. These facts check all geometric hypotheses for the compact-support and projective-line results used below.

source.place: Proof, standard affine-line compactification and factorization into successive affine-line projections

proof.text: For a Noetherian base $T$ on which $N$ is invertible, write $j:\mathbf A^1_T\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^1_T$, $q:\mathbf P^1_T\to T$, and $p=qj$. The map $j$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. It is separated because its diagonal is an isomorphism. It is finite type: over each affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq T$, on each of the two standard affine charts of $\mathbf P^1_R$, its preimage is either the whole chart or the principal open obtained by inverting the other coordinate, whose coordinate ring is generated by that inverse over the chart ring [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Apply the first assertion of [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] to this separated finite-type etale map. It gives $Dj_!\dashv j^*$ on the whole unbounded categories. Here the etale sum extension in that assertion is exactly ordinary open extension by zero, by the open-immersion clause of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension]. No bounded-below restriction or assertion about a chosen exceptional adjoint is used.

source.place: Proof, the open-immersion adjunction in the standard compactification

proof.text:
With this compactification, [def-amb-etale-compact-support] gives $Rp_!\cong Rq_*Dj_!$, using [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] to identify the compactification candidate with $Rp_!$. The coefficient and base hypotheses are exactly those of [thm-amb-p1-adjunction]. For every $M\in D((\mathbf A^1_T)_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $K\in D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, its adjunction and Step 2 give natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(Rp_!M,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Dj_!M,q^*K(1)[2])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,j^*(q^*K(1)[2])).$$
By [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] the last target is $j^*q^*K(1)[2]$. The module-linear inverse-image composition isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear] identifies $j^*q^*$ with $p^*$ termwise; exactness [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] makes this an isomorphism on arbitrary complexes after localization. Hence the bijections exhibit $Rp_!\dashv p^*(-)(1)[2]$ for every base $T$ above. Equivalently this is the composite adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction].

source.place: Proof, affine-line adjunction obtained from the projective-line and open adjunctions

proof.text:
Record the elementary twist calculation used in the induction. By [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line], every nonnegative $A_T(r)$ is flat. Thus the derived twist of a complex $C$ is computed by $C\otimes_A A_T(r)$ itself: a K-flat resolution $P\to C$ from [def-kun-derived-tensor] stays a quasi-isomorphism after tensoring with this flat sheaf, since the exact tensor functor preserves kernels, images and cohomology. Applying [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] moves twists and shifts through any inverse image. On representing complexes, the map
$$(C\otimes_A A_T(r))\otimes_A A_T(1)\longrightarrow C\otimes_A A_T(r+1)$$
is $((c\otimes(l_1\otimes\cdots\otimes l_r))\otimes l)\mapsto c\otimes(l_1\otimes\cdots\otimes l_r\otimes l)$, with the inverse regrouping factors, using the tensor-power definition [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. The case $r=0$ is the scalar-unit map and its inverse. The Tate factors have degree zero, so these maps commute with differentials and are natural in $C$. The shifts $[2r]$ and $[2]$ combine to $[2r+2]$ directly from $C[b]^n=C^{n+b}$, with differential sign $(-1)^{2r+2}=1$. Consequently $(K(r)[2r])(1)[2]\cong K(r+1)[2r+2]$ naturally, on unbounded complexes too.

source.place: Proof, sentence that the twists add; explicit flat-tensor and even-shift calculation

proof.text: For $d=0$, [def-sbc-affine-space] identifies $p_0$ with the identity of $S$. Choose the compactification $(1_S,1_S)$ in [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Both extension by zero along the identity and its derived direct image are identity functors: termwise they do nothing, and localization sends a resolution quasi-isomorphism to an isomorphism. The compactification-independence isomorphism of [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] identifies this candidate with $Rp_{0!}$, hence $Rp_{0!}\cong\operatorname{id}$. Also $p_0^*K(0)[0]\cong K$, since $A_S(0)=A_S$ [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist] and tensoring with this free rank-one coefficient sheaf is the scalar-unit identification of Step 4. The identity adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] proves the assertion.

Inductively suppose $Rp_{r!}\dashv G_r$, where $G_r(K)=p_r^*K(r)[2r]$. Step 3 applied to $T=X_r$ gives $Ra_{r+1,!}\dashv H_{r+1}$ with $H_{r+1}(L)=a_{r+1}^*L(1)[2]$. Since $p_{r+1}=p_ra_{r+1}$, the unbounded composition isomorphism of [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] and the composite-adjunction bijections [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] yield, for arbitrary $M$ on $X_{r+1}$ and $K$ on $S$,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(Rp_{r+1,!}M,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Rp_{r!}Ra_{r+1,!}M,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Ra_{r+1,!}M,G_rK)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,H_{r+1}G_rK).$$
The pullback-of-twist formula [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] and the module inverse-image composition isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear], applied termwise using [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], identify this last right-adjoint object with
$$H_{r+1}G_rK\cong\bigl(p_{r+1}^*K(r)[2r]\bigr)(1)[2]\cong p_{r+1}^*K(r+1)[2r+2],$$
where the second isomorphism is the explicit calculation of Step 4. Every displayed bijection and isomorphism is natural in both arguments. Thus the inductive claim holds for $r+1$, and Step 5 starts the induction. This proves the stated adjunction for every $d$ on the entire ordinary unbounded categories.

blueprint_update.statement:
For $p_d:\mathbf A^d_S\to S$, on the entire ordinary
derived categories of etale $A$-module sheaves,

$$
Rp_{d!}\dashv p_d^*(d)[2d].
$$

proof.text:
Let $j:\mathbf A^1_S\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^1_S$.
The definition in [def-amb-etale-compact-support]
is $Rp_{1!}=Rq_*j_!$. By
[thm-amb-p1-adjunction], [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality],
its right adjoint is $j^*q^*(1)[2]=p_1^*(1)[2]$.
For $d=0$ the assertion is the identity adjunction.
The composition of compact-support functors is
[lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]. For $d>0$, factor the affine-space projection into
$d$ successive affine-line projections. The right
adjoint of the composite is the reversed composite of
their right adjoints, by their Hom adjunction bijections.
The twists add by [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], giving
$p_d^*(d)[2d]$.
